title: ESP32-S3 DevKitC, one USB port through a wall
summary: The S3 DevKitC (and its YD-ESP32-S3 clone) has no mounting holes and two USB ports. It sits on a taped pedestal between its pin rows in an outline pocket. Only one port comes through the wall, flush; the other stays behind a skin of wall so nothing gets plugged into the wrong one.

views.label: In the box
views.caption: YD clone, right-hand port open (seen from outside). Turn it round: the open port sits 0.62 back from the outside, the other has a blind pocket behind 0.47 of wall. Drag the slider to pull the board back. To fit it for real, tip it nose-down and lay it onto the tape.

views.label: On a carrier
views.caption: A 7 × 3 carrier, made for a 2.4 wall (not drawn: its inner face is the plate's left edge, where the lip is). The board sits on a frame pedestal between its pin rows, 8 up so the pins, which point down 7.7, end just above the plate. In the box the USB end goes into the wall's socket pocket first, then the back end is pressed down: drag the slider. Its edge rides the two hooks' lead-ins either side of the module and they snap over it; the stop under the module takes the plug's push. To take it out, lift the back of the board by the module (the hooks cam open) and draw the socket out of the wall.

views.label: Fit piece
views.caption: The USB end of four holders on one strip of 2.4 wall, marked 1 to 4 dots: the open port's face 0.62, 0.8 and 1.0 back from the outside, and the tape squashed to 0.7.

specs.note: The lip's outer face is the plate's edge: place the carrier's grid so it lands on the wall's inner face, and cut the wall with s3CarrierWallCut() at the same place. Hooks at 9.0 need no flex relief (2.9 % strain, about 11 N each).

checks: Tip the board in: does the open socket go into its pocket and the board lay level on the tape?
Is the open socket centred in its pocket?
Plug a cable in: does it seat fully and click with the face that far back?
Is the skin over the closed port whole and stiff enough, and does that port clear its pocket?
